name: @aitherium/bead-space
description: Embeddable force-graph universe — nodes as planets, dependencies as flight paths, active owners as orbiting/patrolling ships. Framework-agnostic core + React wrapper + AitherOS data adapters.
_entrypoints: Top-level entries point at SOURCE, publishConfig points at dist/ — the convention desktop-core, calendar-kit and creative-core use. AitherVeil lists this package in transpilePackages and compiles the TS itself, and the Veil image copies the directory in WITHOUT running its build, so a dist/ path here resolves only on a machine where someone ran `npm run build` by hand. When the package directory was deleted and restored from git, dist/ (gitignored build output) did not come back and every consumer broke with `Can't resolve '@aitherium/bead-space'`. npm swaps publishConfig in at publish time, so the published package is unchanged.

scripts.demo: npm run demo:data && npm run demo:build && python -m http.server 8099 --bind 127.0.0.1
scripts.test: esbuild test/ecosystem.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --outfile=test/ecosystem.mjs --external:jsdom && node test/ecosystem.mjs && esbuild test/smoke.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --outfile=test/smoke.mjs --external:jsdom && node test/smoke.mjs
scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run test
